=== 35e118d ===
35e118d fix(run): reject malformed/ignored ROI boundary specs
Two ways a hybrid run could silently measure the WRONG PC window:

1. --pc-start/--pc-end were accepted with --trigger marker (and dropped),
   so the run measured the marker window, not the pc window the user gave.
   The guards keyed on `model != "hybrid"`; key them on `trigger != "pc"`
   instead, matching their own "applies only to --mode hybrid --trigger pc"
   message. fast/cycle still reject these flags as before.

2. A 0x address with non-hex chars (0xZZZ, 0x10zz) was passed verbatim to
   strtoull, which truncated it to 0x0 / 0x10 -- a wrong but silent enter/exit
   PC. resolve_pc now validates the post-0x chars are all hex, else the
   existing "malformed address" error.

Tests: elf_syms_test gains 0xZZZ / 0x10zz cases; test_andes_sim_f9 asserts
hybrid+marker+--pc-start is rejected ("applies only to").

The plugin now tracks which mask-governed config CSRs (the Andes block,
PMA, the M-ext block, mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl) the guest actually WROTE,

happens once at translation time (csrrw/csrrwi always write; csrrs/csrrc

decoder lives in hybrid/write_mask.h); only instructions that write a
governed CSR get an exec callback, so steady-state code carries zero
instrumentation and the fast leg's speed is unchanged. ucode rides
transport-always: DSP instructions set its sticky OV flag without a CSR
write, so instruction-level tracking cannot see it (like fcsr's fflags).

The driver's --verify consults the oracle's mask and skips unwritten
CSRs: their drained value is only QEMU's reset default, while the
engine re-reads its own RTL reset -- comparing them would false-positive
on every reset-value divergence (msp_bound all-ones vs 0, milmb.IEN 0
vs 1). The hand-maintained exclusion list stays for the hardware-driven
CSRs the mask cannot cover (counters, mdcause, trigger defaults, mnvec).

Covered by a QEMU smoke test: wm_drain writes mxstatus + mcache_ctl
(read-modify-write-same) and only READS mmisc_ctl; the drained mask must
